parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime shows a criminalising state (2-year penalty), active enforcement (2023 mass arrests, seven 1–2 year sentences, a death in detention, 'inciting debauchery' convictions), and head-of-state incitement to stoning that local LGBTQ people describe as a license to kill. This sits within a documented national crisis of torture, arbitrary detention and extrajudicial killings, with no legal recognition, no registered LGBT organisations, no government protection, and advocacy forced into exile. No trans-specific border, facility or care practice is documented, and no post-January-2024 case appears — an sourcing gap, not safety. Absence of documented executions keeps this above the 0.15 anchors, but state-directed threat-framing plus real custodial sentences and impunity place it firmly in High Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No source addresses visa screening, secondary inspection, body-scanner pat-downs, or treatment of a foreign passport's gender marker.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy or presentation-based questioning could plausibly trigger general police contact, then the criminalising and arbitrary-detention regime — but this chain is unevidenced in the dossier.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: 24 arrested March 2023 on same-sex conduct charges with one accused dying in detention; seven convicted of inciting debauchery; seven sentenced August 2023. Broader record shows arbitrary detention, torture and prolonged pretrial detention.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: One 2009 arrest resolved via advocacy intervention; one 2014 case dropped for lack of evidence. No standing remedy documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any outing or document friction escalates into a system where detention itself produced a death and convictions are readily obtained.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No trans-specific facility, custody-placement, ward or strip-search rule appears. General prison conditions are described as harsh and torture is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: If detained, the visitor enters documented harsh prison conditions with no LGBT-specific protection or segregated-placement protocol.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. Nothing on gender-affirming care, medication import, or medical screening for visitors.
care_services.interaction: An emergency could out the visitor to medics inside a state whose broader record includes torture and arbitrary detention, but this is speculative.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented and severe: December 2023 presidential call to take homosexuals to stadiums and stone them, rejection of rights-conditioned aid; LGBTQ residents report terror, an exiled league calls it a call for lynching, members call it a license to kill.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: None documented; no government protection from discrimination (2016 report), no meaningful legal reform (March 2026 entry).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official hostility licenses both state actors and private actors against an outed visitor, and forecloses appealing to authority.

minors_guardians.exposure: Documented: a 15-year-old was sentenced in 2016 with a homosexuality charge layered onto a rape charge, showing the provision is applied to minors and used as a charge-stacking tool.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a minor risks the child being drawn into any proceeding; combined with family-rejection and stigmatisation reporting, this is an open but structurally adverse question.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented at the climate level: 2015 report records arrests and harassment of LGBT persons inside a crisis of extrajudicial killings; 2026 entry lists SGBV, arbitrary arrest and torture; 2023–24 rhetoric described locally as a license to kill.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented. Advocacy organisations cannot register; the rights league operates from exile.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street hostility and official incitement reinforce each other, with no domestic organisation able to assist a visitor who is attacked.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Documented absence of meaningful recourse: no LGR, no registered LGBT associations, no government protection, exiled advocacy, no meaningful legal reform as of March 2026.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Occasional case-level relief only (2009 advocacy intervention, 2014 dismissal).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Article-number discrepancy (567 vs 250), unknown border/care practice, and no documented case after January 2024 leave real uncertainty — a sourcing gap, not evidence of changed conditions.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this anchor's routine border detention, assaults in custody and near-credible capital reach: no documented entry screening, no execution pathway for trans visitors, and occasional case-level relief exists. But the 2023 death in detention plus presidential stoning incitement keep the gap narrow.

Higher exposure than this anchor: Varnalia's record is raids, fines and rare imprisonment with courts sometimes overturning convictions. Here the state itself recently obtained 1–2 year custodial sentences, a death occurred in detention, and the head of state publicly urged stoning, with no functioning domestic remedy.

Substantially lower than this anchor: Karthovia's harm is identity-check harassment without credible imprisonment. This dossier documents actual convictions, mass arrests, custodial death and state-incited violence — custody and lethal threat-framing rather than mere investigative friction.

parsed.synthesis: Law, state rhetoric and practice align against the traveller. Criminalisation (up to two years) is actively enforced — 2023 produced mass arrests, seven 'inciting debauchery' convictions, seven custodial sentences and a death in detention — while the president's stoning call was experienced locally as a license to kill. This operates inside a documented crisis of torture, arbitrary detention and extrajudicial killings, with no registered LGBT organisations, no legal recognition, no government protection and advocacy exiled, so recourse is effectively absent. Border, facility and care practices are undocumented — open questions, not protections — and the silence after January 2024 reflects sourcing gaps. For an adult alone or with a minor, discovery risks imprisonment, custody abuse and state-tolerated violence; rated High Risk, short of the 0.15 tier because no execution or routine street-sweep pattern against trans visitors is documented.
